[ASSISTANT_SAID] The film "Deliverance" explores themes of masculinity and violence through the character of Lewis by portraying him as a hyper-masculine and aggressive individual who believes in male dominance and superiority.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lewis is depicted as a hunter and adventurer who takes pride in his strength and toughness, as shown in the scene where he trains his friends on how to shoot a bow and arrow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lewis's confrontational and violent behavior reinforces the idea that to be a "real man," one must display strength, aggression, and dominance over others.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The film shows the limitations and dangers of extreme masculinity, as Lewis's actions lead to tragic consequences and put himself and his friends in danger.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lewis's behavior can be seen as a manifestation of toxic masculinity and the dangers of living up to gendered stereotypes and expectations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lewis's desire to take risks could stem from wanting to prove his own masculinity and wanting to prove something to his friends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The other characters in the film do not actively challenge Lewis's behavior and often go along with his suggestions, highlighting how toxic masculinity can be perpetuated by passive enabling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ed, the main character, ultimately stands up to Lewis, showing that it is possible to challenge toxic masculinity and its dangerous consequences.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Addressing toxic masculinity is crucial for creating a safer and healthier environment, involving challenging harmful behaviors and promoting positive expressions of masculinity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Creating safe and non-judgmental spaces for discussions about toxic masculinity is essential for education and awareness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Safe spaces can help individuals feel heard, validated, and supported, promoting healing and growth.
